issues.legal_issue: A suit arising from a contract made by a Part C State must name that State, rather than the Union of India, as the defendant when the State is separately administered through an authorized Lieutenant-Governor.
material_facts: The plaintiffs had obtained a contract from the government of the territory to harvest forest produce and later sued for damages and an injunction against recovery of the unpaid contract amount.
The territory was a Part C State administered by the President through a Lieutenant-Governor.
The Lieutenant-Governor was authorized to discharge government functions under the civil procedure rules, and the executive power of the government included dealing with State property.
The plaintiffs named the State as defendant; the challenge that the Union of India was the proper defendant was raised in appeal.
issues.conclusion: The State was the proper defendant, the suit was properly filed against it, and the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 79 of the Code of Civil Procedure, the State is named in a suit against a State Government, whereas the Union of India is named in a suit against the Central Government. The General Clauses Act definitions of “State” (section 3(58)), “Central Government” (section 3(8)), and “State Government” (section 3(60)), read with article 239 of the Constitution, mean that a Part C State remains a distinct State administered through its authorized Lieutenant-Governor; the definition linking its State Government to the Central Government does not make the Union of India the proper defendant. The Lieutenant-Governor’s authority to discharge the relevant government functions and the allocation of executive power under section 38(2) of the Government of Part C States Act support that result. The Court relied on Satya Deo v. Padam Deo, (1955) 1 S.C.R. 549, for the separate existence of Part C States and the distinction between their contracts and contracts with the Central Government.

rule.if: suit_against_government and contract_with_part_c_government and part_c_state_separately_administered and local_administrator_authorized

predicates.suit_against_government: A plaintiff brought a civil suit against a government arising from a government transaction.
predicates.contract_with_part_c_government: The government of a Part C State made the contract at issue in the course of dealing with property or affairs of that State.
predicates.part_c_state_separately_administered: The territory had the separate status of a Part C State and was administered separately from the Union government.
predicates.local_administrator_authorized: The appointed administrator was authorized to perform the relevant government and litigation functions for that State.

issues.definition: When a government suit concerns a contract made by a separately administered Part C State and its appointed administrator was authorized to perform the relevant functions, the State is the proper defendant.
